content.title: About
content.content: Greek nonfat yogurt is a thick, creamy dairy product made by double‑straining regular yogurt. Skim milk is used, and most of the whey is removed, resulting in a higher protein content and a velvety texture. Non‑fruit varieties are typically flavored with vanilla, honey, caramel, or spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greek yogurt, known in Greece as “straggisto,” has been made for centuries.
Double‑straining can raise the protein content to about 10 g per 100 g, nearly double that of regular yogurt.
The nonfat version retains most of milk’s nutrients while containing virtually no fat.
Non‑fruit flavors often rely on natural flavor extracts and modest amounts of low‑calorie sweeteners such as stevia or erythritol.
Greek yogurt is frequently used as a substitute for sour cream or mayonnaise in recipes.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein supports muscle growth and repair and helps promote satiety.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: The near‑zero fat makes it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Skim milk provides a good amount of calcium for bone health, and many products are fortified with vitamin D.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Live cultures such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium help maintain a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The combination of high protein and low sugar leads to a modest impact on blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although some lactose is removed during straining, the product still contains enough to cause symptoms in lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to Greek yogurt.

items.title: Added sweeteners
items.content: Some brands use artificial sweeteners that can cause digestive upset in sensitive persons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy Greek nonfat yogurt on its own, blend it into smoothies, use it as a base for dips, sauces, baked goods, or desserts. It pairs well with nuts, seeds, or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the yogurt refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in its original container. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors, mold, or an unusual texture.
